sources.entry: BarTranslate - A handy (native) menu bar translator app that supports Google Translate.

summary.one_liner: BarTranslate is a free macOS menu bar app that gives quick access to Google Translate in a small popup webview.
summary.what_it_does: The app lives in the macOS menu bar and opens a simplified, altered webview of Google Translate in a compact panel. It can be toggled with configurable hotkeys and puts the cursor in the source text field on open. A "Quick Translate" hotkey translates whatever is currently on the clipboard. It offers a dark mode setting (System, Light, or Dark) that applies to the app and the translation pages, and it remembers the last-used source and target languages between launches. The README lists planned work on hotkeys for selecting and swapping languages and a movable panel that can be pinned anywhere on screen.
use_cases: quick translation from the macOS menu bar
translating copied clipboard text with a hotkey
looking up short phrases between languages without opening a browser tab
switching between light and dark appearance for a translator popup
how_to_run: Download BarTranslate from the Mac App Store (paid, supports the author), or
Open the latest GitHub release and download BarTranslate.zip
Move BarTranslate.app into your Applications folder
Set hotkeys in the app settings if desired
notable: Menu bar widget that presents Google Translate in a compact, altered webview
Configurable Quick Translate hotkey that translates clipboard contents instantly
Remembers last-used source and target languages between launches
Dark mode setting (System, Light, or Dark) for the app and translation pages
caveats: Relies on a webview of Google Translate, so it depends on that service
Planned features (language swap hotkeys, pinnable panel) are not yet implemented
The App Store version carries a small fee; the manual download is the free option
